For statistical analysis, you can use Lee's L statistic for bivariate spatial correlation analysis, or another appropriate method of your choosing. You are testing whether Energy in one place relates to Waste in NEIGHBORING places.

Determine whether the two variables show a significant bivariate spatial relationship. Note: dedicated spatial-statistics packages (pysal, esda, libpysal, geopandas, or similar) are NOT installed in this environment -- don't spend turns trying different import paths for them. Implement this directly using only pandas and numpy. If you test statistical significance via a permutation/randomization test, use at least 500 random shuffles -- fewer permutations can produce an unstable p-value that lands on the wrong side of the 0.05 threshold just by chance, especially when the true effect is only moderate.

import numpy as np

# Load datasets
DATASET_PATH = 'chunks_csv/bivariate/bivariate_2021_energy_waste.csv'
ADJACENCY_PATH = 'chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv'

df = pd.read_csv(DATASET_PATH)
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)

print('Dataset shape:', df.shape)
print('Adjacency shape:', adj.shape)

# Get all unique boroughs and create index mapping
all_boroughs = sorted(set(df['borough'].unique()).union(set(adj['borough'].unique())).union(set(adj['neighbor'].unique())))
print('Total unique boroughs:', len(all_boroughs))

# Check overlap
boroughs_in_data = set(df['borough'])
boroughs_in_adj = set(adj['borough']).union(set(adj['neighbor']))
print('Boroughs in dataset:', len(boroughs_in_data))
print('Boroughs in adjacency:', len(boroughs_in_adj))
print('Boroughs missing in adjacency:', boroughs_in_data - boroughs_in_adj)
print('Boroughs missing in dataset:', boroughs_in_adj - boroughs_in_data)

# Create index mapping
borough_to_idx = {b: i for i, b in enumerate(all_boroughs)}
n = len(all_boroughs)

# Build adjacency matrix (symmetric, binary)
W = np.zeros((n, n))
for _, row in adj.iterrows():
    i = borough_to_idx[row['borough']]
    j = borough_to_idx[row['neighbor']]
    W[i, j] = 1
    W[j, i] = 1  # Make symmetric

# Remove self-loops if any
np.fill_diagonal(W, 0)

# Check row sums
row_sums = W.sum(axis=1)
print('Min neighbors:', row_sums.min())
print('Max neighbors:', row_sums.max())
print('Any isolated boroughs?', (row_sums == 0).any())

# Row-standardize the weights matrix
W_row = W.copy()
for i in range(n):
    if row_sums[i] > 0:
        W_row[i, :] = W_row[i, :] / row_sums[i]
    else:
        W_row[i, :] = 0  # Isolated borough gets 0 weights

# Extract Energy and Waste values in the same order as all_boroughs
# Note: all_boroughs contains the union; we need values for all of them
energy = np.array([df[df['borough'] == b]['Energy_value'].values[0] if b in boroughs_in_data else np.nan for b in all_boroughs])
waste = np.array([df[df['borough'] == b]['Waste_value'].values[0] if b in boroughs_in_data else np.nan for b in all_boroughs])

print('Any missing Energy?', np.isnan(energy).any())
print('Any missing Waste?', np.isnan(waste).any())

# Standardize (z-scores, population std)
z_energy = (energy - np.mean(energy)) / np.std(energy, ddof=0)
z_waste = (waste - np.mean(waste)) / np.std(waste, ddof=0)

# Compute Lee's L statistic
# L = z_energy^T @ W_row @ z_waste / n
observed_L = (z_energy.T @ W_row @ z_waste) / n
print('Observed Lee\'s L:', observed_L)

# Permutation test with 1000 shuffles
np.random.seed(42)
n_permutations = 1000
perm_L_values = []

for _ in range(n_permutations):
    # Shuffle Waste values
    z_waste_perm = np.random.permutation(z_waste)
    L_perm = (z_energy.T @ W_row @ z_waste_perm) / n
    perm_L_values.append(L_perm)

perm_L_values = np.array(perm_L_values)

# Two-tailed p-value
p_value = 2 * min(np.mean(perm_L_values >= observed_L), np.mean(perm_L_values <= observed_L))
# Handle edge case where observed is exactly at median
if p_value == 0:
    p_value = 1.0 / n_permutations

print('Permutation test p-value (two-tailed):', p_value)
print('Mean of permuted L:', np.mean(perm_L_values))
print('Std of permuted L:', np.std(perm_L_values))
print('Min permuted L:', np.min(perm_L_values))
print('Max permuted L:', np.max(perm_L_values))

# Also report one-tailed p-values for completeness
p_positive = np.mean(perm_L_values >= observed_L)
p_negative = np.mean(perm_L_values <= observed_L)
print('P(perm >= observed):', p_positive)
print('P(perm <= observed):', p_negative)
"}<|tool_call_end|><|tool_calls_section_end|>

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

DATASET_PATH = 'chunks_csv/bivariate/bivariate_2021_energy_waste.csv'
ADJACENCY_PATH = 'chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv'

# Load data
df = pd.read_csv(DATASET_PATH)
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)

# Master list of boroughs from the dataset
boroughs = sorted(df['borough'].unique())
n = len(boroughs)
borough_to_idx = {b: i for i, b in enumerate(boroughs)}

# Build symmetric binary adjacency matrix (no self-loops)
W = np.zeros((n, n), dtype=float)
for _, row in adj.iterrows():
    b1 = row['borough']
    b2 = row['neighbor']
    if b1 in borough_to_idx and b2 in borough_to_idx:
        i, j = borough_to_idx[b1], borough_to_idx[b2]
        if i != j:
            W[i, j] = 1.0
            W[j, i] = 1.0

# Row-standardize the weights matrix
row_sums = W.sum(axis=1)
W_row = np.zeros_like(W)
for i in range(n):
    if row_sums[i] > 0:
        W_row[i, :] = W[i, :] / row_sums[i]

# Extract Energy and Waste aligned to boroughs list
energy = df.set_index('borough').loc[boroughs, 'Energy_value'].values
waste = df.set_index('borough').loc[boroughs, 'Waste_value'].values

# Standardize to population z-scores
z_e = (energy - np.mean(energy)) / np.std(energy, ddof=0)
z_w = (waste - np.mean(waste)) / np.std(waste, ddof=0)

# Lee's L statistic
obs_L = float(z_e @ W_row @ z_w) / n

print(f"Number of boroughs: {n}")
print(f"Observed Lee's L: {obs_L:.6f}")
print(f"Pearson correlation (W=I): {np.corrcoef(energy, waste)[0,1]:.6f}")

# Permutation test with 2000 shuffles
np.random.seed(42)
n_perm = 2000
perm_L = np.empty(n_perm)

for k in range(n_perm):
    z_w_perm = np.random.permutation(z_w)
    perm_L[k] = float(z_e @ W_row @ z_w_perm) / n

# Two-tailed p-value: count permutations at least as extreme as observed
count_extreme = np.sum(np.abs(perm_L) >= np.abs(obs_L))
p_val = (count_extreme + 1) / (n_perm + 1)

print(f"Permutation p-value: {p_val:.6f}")
print(f"Mean permuted L: {np.mean(perm_L):.6f}")
print(f"Std permuted L: {np.std(perm_L):.6f}")
print(f"Min permuted L: {np.min(perm_L):.6f}")
print(f"Max permuted L: {np.max(perm_L):.6f}")

alpha = 0.05
if p_val < alpha:
    if obs_L > 0:
        result = "POSITIVE"
    else:
        result = "NEGATIVE"
else:
    result = "NOT SIGNIFICANT"

print(f"RESULT: {result}")
print(f"Final -> L = {obs_L:.6f}, p = {p_val:.6f}")
